story.title: Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic

facts.text: Trust isn't the only factor in winning the agentic AI space, but it's a start.
The next step is, of course, for Apple to design Siri to work better within third-party apps to complete autonomous tasks.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) launched a new version of Siri just last month, and it's undoubtedly the best version of the personal agent the company has ever released.

Siri can now interact like other artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots by answering more in-depth questions; it also has on-screen awareness and more personal context than before because it can search through photos, emails, and texts.
Most of my personal devices are Apple products, and I've been less than enthused by Siri for years now.
The latest update was a big leap forward, but it essentially caught Apple up with where OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude were several years ago.
If Apple is in the same place it is now a year from now, after the next iteration of Siri has presumably debuted, Apple's AI software miss could turn into a hardware sales problem.
But as helpful as all of this is, just a few weeks after its launch, Siri still feels dated.

With the recent launch of Meta Platforms ' (NASDAQ: META) popular Muse app , which can autonomously complete personal tasks such as booking a flight and shopping online, it's clear that Siri still doesn't measure up.
Apple is expected to push Siri to become more agentic and enable features that will allow it to perform ongoing tasks, not just one-offs.

Apple ultimately wants to go in this direction, I’m told, and I believe the company could make Siri more like an agent as early as next year — not that it has much of a choice, given current consumer and market demands.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI czar Craig Federighi to accelerate the Siri roadmap and deliver a powerful AI agent that can compete with OpenAI’s Dots or Meta’s Muse.
Two significant improvements are expected to be made to Siri in the coming months.
One will give the assistant fine-grained control over Apple’s first-party apps, allowing it to do things like rotate and crop images in Photos and organize Safari tabs.
That would let Siri place an order through Grubhub or book a dinner reservation through OpenTable, for example.

Apple CEO John Ternus is putting intense pressure on AI chief Craig Federighi to transform Siri into a full-fledged agentic assistant capable of competing with OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman.
If third-party apps optimize for OpenAI and Meta agents first, Apple risks becoming a second-class citizen in the AI ecosystem it desperately wants to control.

While Federighi's team managed to ship a working version of Siri AI on what insiders describe as an "incredibly short timeline," Apple executives privately admit they're not keeping pace with rivals who've already deployed AI agents capable of autonomous, multi-step tasks.
Meta, meanwhile, has been aggressively rolling out Muse across its family of apps, giving billions of users access to agentic capabilities.
The company needs Siri to become genuinely useful - not just incrementally better - to keep developers building for Apple Intelligence first.
Users expect agents that anticipate needs, coordinate complex workflows, and actually save time - capabilities that require fundamentally different architectures than what Siri was built on.
Apple's internal urgency around Siri signals a broader shift in how the company views AI competition.
But relying on OpenAI for core assistant functionality undermines Apple's ecosystem lock-in and puts user data in third-party hands - exactly the scenario Cupertino has spent decades avoiding.

The key insight: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported on November 8 that Apple wants to make Siri more agent-like, possibly as early as next year in Gurman’s view, contrasting Siri’s request-based actions with ChatGPT Dots, Meta Muse and Grok, which Gurman said keep working between conversations.
Apple also gave engineers six weeks of coding instead of four in the first iOS 28 milestone, which by our arithmetic is 50% more coding time in that stage.
The same newsletter reported that Apple changed how it builds its 2027 operating systems.
Apple has not announced an agentic Siri or a date for one.
We first saw the story in X posts by @markgurman and @choblin29.
Apple is still delivering the Siri overhaul it promised years ago.
Now it is already exploring the architecture that could make that version look obsolete.
Our earlier piece reported Apple opening Siri AI to any app .

Apple finally stepping up to compete in AI with a personal AI agent that rivals Meta Muse, grok bot etc. few thoughts: – the new feature would allow 3rd-party apps to integrate siri. which means siri can perform actions, pull context through every app on your phone. that’s pretty sick. – despite being behind in AI, apple has a huge advantage: 3.5 billion devices people love and use everyday – but at the same time siri right now sucks, is incapable of doing even 30% of the things frontier LLMs can do. it can’t even use a computer. – compare this to muse, dots or grok bot that can work autonomously 24/7, self-improving the more you use it AND have access to their own computer. they’re miles ahead. imo apple has to balance delivering quickly (& aggressively) on AI without causing a major security breach. their whole thing is trust and privacy. that’s the challenge ternus will face.
FOR THE DATES TO WATCH Development of the iOS 28 M2 milestone starts on Monday, the period when Apple will start to finalise what it plans to include, according to Bloomberg.
